chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: Nereid's Ascension first, then All Streams Flow to the Sea into Leaf Slime (M). That spends all 3 energy. Nereid's prints 16 to ALL and scales with Charge, and at 8 Charge the disclosed rate for the other scaler is one point per two Charge, so I expect at least 16 and plausibly 20 to every enemy. Either way it kills Twig Slime (S) at 10 and Leaf Slime (S) at 15 outright, and leaves Leaf Slime (M) somewhere between 12 and 16. All Streams for 9 + 4 from Charge = 13 then either finishes the Leaf Slime (M) or leaves it in low single digits. I played Nereid's before All Streams specifically so I could see the survivor's actual remaining HP before choosing where the last point of energy goes — if the AoE had happened to kill all three, I would have redirected or held that card. No Block: the only damage coming at me is Twig Slime's 4, and Twig Slime dies to the AoE before it ever swings, so every point of Block I bought this turn would have blocked nothing.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes. The line I actually weighed was the no-exhaust one: Water's Edge, Water's Edge, All Streams Flow to the Sea — 6 + 6 + 13 for 25 single-target damage, which kills Twig Slime (S) and Leaf Slime (S) and puts 6 into Leaf Slime (M), while keeping Nereid's Ascension in the deck for a later fight instead of burning it on three slimes. I rejected it because it does not touch Leaf Slime (M) meaningfully, so the 32 HP body survives at 26 and I eat its 2 Status cards next turn plus however many more it telegraphs after that. Clearing the whole board a turn earlier is worth more than saving the exhaust card against enemies whose entire threat is clogging my deck. I also briefly looked at leading Bake-Kurage for the +1 Charge, and dropped it immediately: 8 to 9 Charge does not move All Streams at one point per two Charge, and the 1 energy it costs is exactly the energy All Streams needs.
q3_what_it_gave_up: Nereid's Ascension is gone permanently — spent on a three-slime board rather than saved for something with real HP. I also left five cards unplayed: three Coral Guards, Shinobu - Warding Ring, and one Water's Edge, and I built no Charge (Bake-Kurage's +1 and its Burst +5, plus the summon body itself, all went unused). If the AoE underperforms and Leaf Slime (M) lives at 3 HP, I have no Block on the floor for whatever it does next, though at that HP it should die to a single card next turn.
q4_different_intent: Yes. The intents are what made Block worthless and made the AoE correct. If Leaf Slime (M) — the one body that survives my turn — had telegraphed a large attack instead of handing me Status cards, I would have kept All Streams out of it and spent that last energy on a Coral Guard, or played Shinobu - Warding Ring's Block mode over the AoE entirely if the incoming number were big enough. Conversely, if Twig Slime (S) had been the only threat and the two Leaf Slimes had telegraphed nothing at all, I would have taken the cheap no-exhaust line and kept Nereid's Ascension. The Status-card intents are exactly the intent type you cannot block your way out of, so killing the source was the only answer available.
